title: feat(plugin-auth): a JIT sign-in reads the IdP locale claim into the user language preference
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu6spbcJWyNTVVesWZafpRKR)_

Fixes #25261

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

Claim of record: `6351359330` on the card (card thread, `domain:services` seat 1). Branch `claude/project-thread-6usz2l` is the harness-pinned branch for this session; it names no issue, so the Duplicate Fix Guard's branch-name hint will not match, and the claim is the identity record.

## What changes

When an external IdP sign-in creates or refreshes a user just-in-time, the standard OIDC `locale` claim (OIDC Core 5.1, a BCP-47 tag) now becomes `sys_user.locale`: the column the console reads as the signed-in user's UI language (objectui `useUserLocale`, `LocaleSwitcher`, `ProfilePage`) and service-messaging reads per recipient. On a hosted environment the cloud is the IdP (`oidcProviders`, provider `objectstack-cloud`), so the environment follows the cloud account language. The cloud half (the control plane's OIDC provider emits `locale`) is objectstack-ai/cloud#3159.

The rule (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/idp-locale-claim.ts`, module header):

| sign-in | what happens to `sys_user.locale` |
|:--|:--|
| first creation, supported claim | set to the claim, in the supported spelling |
| later sign-in, the column still holds what the IdP last wrote (or is unset) | follows the claim |
| later sign-in, the user picked a language in the environment | kept: a local choice wins |
| unknown or unsupported claim | left unset (an IdP-written value is cleared), so the deployment default applies |
| no `locale` claim | unchanged |

**Closed against the supported list.** The claim is matched against the locales the i18n service reports (`getLocales()`, which the app's declared `i18n.supportedLocales` narrows) with the platform's own matcher, `resolveLocale` from `@objectstack/core` (exact, case-insensitive, base language, variant), and the SUPPORTED spelling is stored (`zh-cn` stores `zh-CN`, `en-US` stores `en` when `en` is what is supported). The shape check is service-messaging's `normalizeRecipientLocale`, the one reader of a value at rest in the column, so nothing the IdP sends can store a value the readers discard. The underscore spelling OIDC Core 5.1 notes (`zh_CN`) reads as the tag it stands for. With no i18n service to ask, nothing is applied (said once at `warn`): judging without the list would be judging anyway.

**Telling a local choice from an IdP-written value.** The column alone cannot say who wrote it, so the value the IdP path last wrote is recorded beside it: one `sys_verification` row per user (identifier `idp-locale:` plus the user id), written through better-auth's DATABASE adapter, the implicit-linking unlink record's idiom in the same package and for the same reason (a host `secondaryStorage` cache must never be its only home). The IdP owns the column while it is unset or still holds exactly the recorded value. Every partial failure degrades toward "a local choice wins" (the column is written before the record). A deleted user's record is cleared in the composed `user.delete.after`. No schema change, no new column, no new authorable key.

**Where it runs.** better-auth hands the raw IdP profile to the `validateUserInfo` seam on every action of an external sign-in: `source.oauth.profile` for generic-OAuth and social providers, `source.sso.profile` for `@better-auth/sso` OIDC providers (measured in the installed better-auth 1.7.12: `api/routes/callback.mjs`, `oauth2/link-account.mjs`, `db/internal-adapter.mjs`, and `@better-auth/sso` `dist/index.mjs`). That seam may still refuse and runs before the user row exists, so it only STAGES the claim, keyed by the request's endpoint context (a `WeakMap`, the `usersCreatedInRequest` pattern). The session the sign-in mints, new user or returning, settles it in the composed `session.create.after`. A refused sign-in mints no session and the staged claim dies with its request. Applying the claim never fails a sign-in: a store that refuses the write is reported at `warn` (a functional degradation, the user visibly sees the default language) and the user keeps the language they had.

`auth-manager.ts` gains only the three call sites and the instance; the logic is in the new file, so the in-flight move-only split of that file (#25224) and this change merge in either order.

## Pins

`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/idp-locale-claim.test.ts`, 22 cases:

- **Pure (13):** the claim off an `oauth` and an `sso-oidc` source, a present-but-unusable value, no claim for SAML / password / SCIM sources; the supported spelling (exact, case, base, variant), the underscore spelling, unsupported and malformed claims; the decision (creation, following, a local choice wins three ways, an unsupported claim clears only an IdP-written value, a locally cleared column goes back to the IdP, no-op); the deleted-user half.
- **End of the chain (9):** a real better-auth pipeline over the in-memory engine (the `implicit-account-linking.test.ts` harness shape), real OAuth round trips through the platform IdP (`/sign-in/social` then `/callback/objectstack-cloud`, token and userinfo stubbed), reading what landed in `sys_user` and `sys_verification`. The three acceptance cases of the card:
  - a sign-in with `locale: "zh-CN"` creates a user whose `sys_user.locale` is `zh-CN`;
  - a later sign-in with `locale: "en"` after the user picked `ja-JP` locally keeps `ja-JP`;
  - an unsupported `locale` (`fr-FR`) leaves the column unset;
  and following (`zh-CN` then `en-US` stores `en`), an unsupported claim clearing an IdP-written value but never a local one, no claim changing nothing, a pre-existing local value kept, a user store that refuses the write (sign-in still lands, `warn`), and no i18n service (nothing written, one `warn`).

One-time proofs (not left as tests), each in `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor must hit once, blob must move, restore proven: blob equal to HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty). The subject is imported from source, so there is no `dist/` leg.

| leg | what is undone | file reading |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | the `settle` call in `session.create.after` | 5 failed / 17 passed: acceptance 1, following, no claim, store refusal, no i18n |
| 2 | the local-choice guard in `decideIdpLocaleWrite` | 4 failed / 18 passed: acceptance 2, the pure local-choice cell, unsupported-never-clears-local, pre-existing local value |
| 3 | the supported-list closing in `resolveIdpLocale` (raw tag stored) | 5 failed / 17 passed: acceptance 3, the two pure closing cells, following, unsupported-clears |

- **Not run locally, declared to CI:** the type-check lanes and the path-scheduled CI jobs `dispatch-gates` names. No dogfood battery is owed (no `!` in the title, no `(narrowing)` arm).

The generated regions come from `node scripts/tenant-audit-census.mjs --write`; the hand-written figures the gate holds to the census (six places on the page) were moved by hand to the census's new figures, and `check-tenant-audit-census` is green.

These three paths sit outside the claim's declared file surface; they are the gates' own ledgers for the declared change, not a widening.

## Acceptance notes

- Social providers are OAuth sign-ins too, so a Google sign-in that carries `locale` sets the preference the same way; SAML sign-ins carry no standard locale claim and are not read.
- A user who picks the very language the IdP asserts is indistinguishable from one who never picked, and keeps following the IdP; clearing the column locally hands it back to the IdP. Both follow from "the IdP owns the column while it holds what the IdP last wrote".
- The alternative to the `sys_verification` record is a provenance column on `sys_user` (a `platform-objects` change in another lane); the record keeps the change inside `plugin-auth` with no schema change. Either way the behaviour above is the same.
